2026-06-09 · Preprint · medRxiv/bioRxiv

Critical dynamics in spontaneous EEG predict perturbational complexity in disorders of consciousness with measurable evoked responses

Newman D, Maschke C, O'Byrne J, Colombo MA, Comanducci A, Casarotto S, Citerio G, Rosanova M, Massimini M, Jerbi K, Blain-Moraes S

Resting brain signals could stand in for the stimulation-based consciousness index in some brain-injured patients, but not across all of them.

The best-tested consciousness index needs a magnetic pulse to the head. This team asked whether ordinary resting EEG can predict it in 26 brain-injured patients. It could not across the whole group, only in patients whose injury was not from lack of oxygen and in those with a measurable response.

26 patients (vascular, traumatic, anoxic). Multivariate criticality features did not generalise PCImax prediction across the full cohort; they did when restricted to non-anoxic patients and to patients with non-zero PCImax. Extends Maschke et al. 2024 (anaesthesia) to brain injury. Not peer reviewed.

What we do with it

Tempers the 2024 claim that resting EEG can replace PCI. Our out-of-sample test of that claim should report results by aetiology. Planned

Read the original. Source checked against the original.
